prose.hook: Scattered across the North Pacific roughly halfway between Hawaii and Australia, the Marshall Islands consists of 29 atolls and five isolated islands arranged in two nearly parallel chains, the Ratak and the Ralik, totaling about 1,225 islands and islets, most of them uninhabited. Kwajalein atoll encloses the world's largest lagoon, and the nearby island city of Ebeye ranks as one of the most densely populated spots in the Pacific. The country has no land borders with any nation.
prose.physicalGeography: The islands are low coral limestone and sand formations, offering little elevation above sea level. They are grouped into two almost-parallel chains, the Ratak, or Sunrise, group and the Ralik, or Sunset, group, comprising 29 atolls and five isolated islands out of roughly 1,225 islands and islets in total. Of these, 22 of the atolls and four of the islands are uninhabited.
prose.climate: The climate is tropical, hot and humid year-round, with a wet season running from May to November. The islands lie within the typhoon belt, though typhoons occur only infrequently.
prose.economy: The Marshall Islands is classified as an upper middle-income Pacific island economy that relies heavily on aid from the United States and supports a large public sector. Coconut oil is produced as a substitute for diesel fuel, and the country has developed a growing offshore banking sector alongside income from selling fishing rights, while remaining dependent on imports. Key industries include copra, tuna processing, tourism, and craft items made from seashells, wood, and pearls, and recent exports include ships, refined petroleum, fish, natural gas, and stone processing machines.
prose.peopleAndCulture: The population is overwhelmingly Marshallese, at 95.6%, with Filipinos and other groups making up the remainder. Christianity dominates religious life, led by Protestant denominations at 79.3%, including the United Church of Christ, Assembly of God, and several smaller churches, alongside Roman Catholics at 9.3% and members of the Church of Jesus Christ at 5.7%.
